scope.summary: Implement the skeletal mesh export core per Section 13.26 via the glTF writer (the PRIMARY lane per the file-format strategy): skinned body with skeleton, skinning weights, and selected morph targets chosen by morph-export-rules, validating against the glTF 2.0 spec and the known UE 5.4 morph-corruption caveat.
acceptance_criteria: glTF export emits the body as a skinned mesh (skins + joints + inverse bind matrices) with the canonical BodyKit skeleton and morph targets for every channel/corrective selected by the profile's morph-export-rules list (Morph-Export-Rules parity).
Output passes glTF 2.0 structural validation in CI (validator or equivalent conformance checks) for a base body and an archetype-extreme body.
A headless-Blender import fixture confirms weights and morph targets (shape keys) survive with correct names and ranges.

The validation report records the UE 5.4.x native glTF morph-corruption caveat when the target profile is ue_gltf (format-strategy documented risk), steering UE users to the FBX-bridge lane when morph fidelity is critical.
Export is deterministic: identical body + profile yields byte-identical glTF (modulo generator timestamp field, which is fixed in tests).
scope.risk_if_missed: The primary interchange lane is broken or lossy, so every downstream profile (Blender, UE, the FBX bridge which consumes glTF) inherits corrupt weights or missing morphs.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
